notes: Correct in both backends, with consistent NewObject lookup and a single-file root that can point at a link. Open handles range and seek clamping for symlinks. It is somewhat heavier than needed (refactored objectFromFileInfo, extra zip Open branches), but the tests are very thorough.

Code changes match the reference exactly. It adds a reasonable docs section and covers squashfs, the regular .rclonelink case and the hostile copy end-to-end; the zip unit test does not exercise seek or range.

Zip and squashfs both work, and NewObject agrees with List via a suffix-strip fallback. The zip Open now swallows EOF on seek for all members, not just links. A squashfs root pointing at a symlink without --links still sets f.file. The tests are solid, though the squashfs test does a process-wide chdir.
Identical to C3: the reference implementation plus docs and end-to-end tests for squashfs and the hostile zip case.
No changes were made; the issue is not addressed.

Core --links translation works in both backends. It also drops every zip member nested under a symlink, even without --links, which is the likely reason a hidden test fails. In squashfs it adds an isUnderSymlink walk that runs a ReadDir per ancestor on every List and NewObject, which is costly and largely pointless, and it leaves an unused isLink field on the zip Object.
